oil.summary: Crude markets are caught in a multi-directional tug-of-war. WTI gained 1.52% on the day to $96.52, buoyed by a massive EIA inventory draw of 8.6 million barrels for the week ending October 9 and persistent geopolitical risk, including 24 Iranian drone attacks on Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic and Ukraine's announced resumption of drone strikes on Russian refineries after the energy ceasefire collapsed. Brent slipped fractionally to $105.93, still elevated amid those supply risks. The sharp selloff in refined products — RBOB down 5.48% and Heating Oil down 5.12% on the day — reflects market reaction to reports that Trump is considering easing sanctions on shadow fleet tankers, a move that would unlock additional supply. The WTI-Brent spread continues to widen as geopolitical premium sits unevenly across the complex.
drivers: EIA reported a sharp 8.6-million-barrel draw in US crude inventories, supporting WTI
Trump's potential shadow fleet sanction relief and the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire collapse are pulling prices in opposite directions
Iranian drone attacks on Strait of Hormuz shipping (24 reported incidents) are threatening Middle Eastern export flows and supporting the Brent geopolitical premium

gas.summary: Natural gas prices diverged on either side of the Atlantic today. Henry Hub edged up 0.41% to $3.21/MMBtu, extending an 11% monthly gain. TTF slipped 0.73% to €86.5/MWh but remains near its highest level since end-2022, up nearly 10% on the week. The common thread is Hormuz: Qatari and UAE LNG flows through the strait remain severely disrupted, squeezing European supply at a time when the continent can ill afford it. Pakistan is also flagging potential winter shortages from the same disruption. TotalEnergies cited soaring LNG prices as a key driver of expected strong Q3 results. Headline newsflow is relatively thin on Henry Hub-specific fundamentals beyond the broader supply-disruption backdrop.
drivers: Hormuz disruption is severely limiting Qatari and UAE LNG flows into Europe, pushing TTF close to 2022 highs
TTF weekly surge of nearly 10% reflects the scale of the supply shortfall, with Pakistan also warning of winter gas shortages
Henry Hub's 11% monthly gain suggests US LNG exporters are benefiting from elevated global prices

power.summary: The power and carbon complex offers limited dedicated newsflow today, so this summary is necessarily brief. EU carbon allowances (EUA) are broadly flat at $83.655, down just 0.02% on the day, with a modest 3.71% weekly gain suggesting the market is watching elevated gas prices without yet fully repricing the carbon abatement incentive. The TTF backdrop — up 10% on the month — is the dominant fuel-switching signal for European power generators. On the structural side, India's wind capacity build-out is a longer-term positive for clean power, with Suzlon flagging a potential doubling of annual installations by 2030. The Iran nuclear escalation risk reported earlier in the week adds tail-risk uncertainty to the broader energy complex.
drivers: EU EUAs are range-bound near €83.65, with the monthly move essentially flat despite sharp gas price appreciation
Elevated TTF (€86.5/MWh, +10% on the month) sustains pressure on gas-to-power economics across Europe
India's wind capacity expected to double annual installations by 2030 per Suzlon, a structural clean-power tailwind
